patterns: The pattern turned into generated code is the one Dual.lean wrote by hand 44 times: a time-reversal iff restated as two forward rules, one guarded by the rule pattern Causality.dual C. It is now one emitter (emit_dual) driven by one key per node. Files it shortens: Causal/Ladder/Dual.lean (321 hand-written lines become 297 generated ones, at the switch), and the 534 campaign-generated examples of DualTest.lean (dual_closure.py, which read Rules.lean's comment lines) become emit-lean's output. No Lean lemma or macro was added to Causal/Ladder or Causal/Tactic in this target.
aesop_limits: The builder shape of an introduction (a theorem (hf : C.P) (hp : C.dual.P) : C.Q) is unit-tested in Python only: the library has no lemma of that shape, so it was not compiled.

Lean does not check the orientation of an iff key in the generated rules. `K.2 h` proves `P C` from `P C.dual` as well as `K.1 h` does, because C.dual.dual is C by rfl. The Python shape check refuses a reversed iff (L must mention dual, R must not) and a lemma about another definition: the node's name must occur as a whole word, or followed by `On` only (since fix round 1, which closed the audit's prefix-match finding). These are textual readings of lean_index's signatures, heuristic by design. The compile is the arbiter.

The def introduction `⟨hf, hp⟩` relies on the definition unfolding to `C.P ∧ C.dual.P`. Python cannot see the body, so only the compile checks it. It does hold for LocallyCausallyOpen and CausallyOpen.

The generated tests model at most one time reversal (literals of C and C.dual). Double reversals, standing instances and conjunctive goals stay in the 27 hand-written examples of DualTest.lean, which the emitter does not write.

dual_contradictions can fire only when the library proves a key's lemma and the ladder records a counterexample against it, that is when the ladder itself is wrong. Its fixture therefore appends a counterexample that is false on purpose.
kb_proposals: programme/ladder.toml's `dual` key (T-tac-ladder-dual-key): a two-sided node names its time-reversal lemma (`dual = "Causal.Causality.dual_isCausal"`, an iff C.dual.P ↔ C.P or C.P → C.dual.P); a one-sided node names what it introduces (`dual = { introduces = "causally_open", lemma = "Causal.Causality.causallyOpen_iff" }`). emit-lean writes Causal/Ladder/Dual.lean and DualTest.lean from the keys, never over a hand-written file (first line not GENERATED): to switch, remove the hand-written file, then run emit-lean.

In a generated rule from an implication `K : C.P → C.dual.P`, `p_of_dual` is `(K h :)`: the empty ascription elaborates `K h` before unifying with `P C`, and C.dual.dual is C by rfl. The same rfl makes `K.2 h` prove `P C` from `P C.dual`, so Lean does not catch a reversed iff key; tools/ladder.py's shape check does.

DualTest.lean is hand-written: kept ...`. The master's emit-lean in that wave changes no file. The switch does not happen in the keeper's wave, and no Lean rebuild is needed.
An introduction and the key of the node it introduces must be written together: an introduction of a keyless node is refused (`carries no two-sided dual key`).
